slot.brief: A short sentence split into parts (A/B/C/D) with a clear subject-verb agreement error; students identify the erroneous part.

stem:
In the following sentence, identify the part that contains a grammatical error.

Neither of the two candidates **(1)** / were present **(2)** / at the interview **(3)** / yesterday. **(4)**

verdicts.working: “Neither” is singular here, so the verb should be “was,” not “were.” The error is in Part 2.

working:
Subject is 'Neither', which is always singular; the phrase 'of the two candidates' is only a prepositional modifier and cannot make it plural. Hence the verb must be singular: 'was present'. Part 2 wrongly uses 'were present' → error in Part 2 (B). Parts 1, 3 and 4 are error-free, so A, C and D are wrong.

Independent check: “Neither” is singular here, so the verb should be “was,” not “were.” The error is in Part 2.
solution: “Neither” is singular, and “of the two candidates” does not change the subject’s number. The verb should be “was present,” not “were present”; hence the error is in Part 2.
